2609.11769.title: Recognizing Is Not Reversing: A Controlled Inversion Test of Fact-Preserving News Framing
2609.11769.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to analyze and rewrite news, yet current framing studies mainly evaluate generation, detection, or whether rewritten text appears more neutral. They do not directly show whether a model can undo a known framing transformation while keeping the facts fixed. We introduce a controlled inversion test over three established textual realizations of framing: evaluative lexis, agency realization, and information salience. Across 60 news articles and three intervention strengths, this yields 540 paired variants with preserved atomic facts and recorded edits. Across Qwen, DeepSeek, and Kimi, factual preservation remains near 0.84, whereas intervention reversal is 0.044--0.068. Even when both framing type and direction are recognized correctly, pooled reversal reaches 0.071. These results reveal a clear separation between factual fidelity, framing recognition, and framing inversion: recognizing how an article is framed does not imply that the framing can be undone.
2609.11769.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地用於分析和改寫新聞，然而目前的框架研究主要評估生成、檢測或改寫文本是否顯得更中立。它們並未直接顯示模型是否能在保持事實不變的情況下撤銷已知的框架轉換。我們引入了一個控制的反轉測試，針對三種已建立的框架文本實現：評價詞彙、代理實現和信息顯著性。在60篇新聞文章和三種干預強度下，這產生了540對保存原子事實和記錄編輯的變體。在Qwen、DeepSeek和Kimi中，事實保存率保持在接近0.84，而干預反轉率為0.044至0.068。即使在框架類型和方向都被正確識別的情況下，合併反轉達到0.071。這些結果揭示了事實忠實度、框架識別和框架反轉之間的明顯區別：識別一篇文章的框架並不意味著該框架可以被撤銷。
2609.11769.author: Yi Liu et.al.
